dashboard.title: Which dashboard?
dashboard.description:
Pick the dashboard to publish.

Tip: create one just for the public, with only what strangers may see. Only dashboards you have saved at least once appear here.

data.name: Who is this link for? (your own note)

path.title: Public address
path.description:
This is the address you will share. Visitors open it with **no login**:

**{base_url}/**`public-path`

For example, with `solar` the page will be at `{base_url}/solar`.

Use lowercase letters, digits and underscores, with no hyphen: that way it can never clash with one of your dashboards.

Every entry of this integration is one link. A link can end by itself: after a span of time counted from now, or on a date. Leave both empty for a link that lasts until you switch it off.

data_description.valid_for: The boxes are days, hours, minutes, seconds. For example 7 in the first box for a week. When set, it replaces the date below and counts from the moment you save.
data_description.expires_at: Empty: the link does not end by itself. From that moment the address answers 'not found' and everyone looking is disconnected.

view.title: Which views?
view.description: A dashboard can have several views: the tabs at the top of **{dashboard}**. Pick the ones that become public; visitors move between them with the same tabs. Every view you leave out stays private and is not even sent to the visitor's browser.

more.title: What else?
more.description: Besides its main dashboard a link can show further dashboards, Home Assistant's Energy dashboard and Frigate's own interface. Visitors move between them with the sidebar. Each gets its own address: the link's, an underscore, and its name.

data.frigate_ui_url: Frigate's address for signing in (its port 8971)
data.frigate_ui_user: Frigate user that visitors look as

data_description.more_dashboards: Each is shown whole unless you choose its views in the next step.
data_description.frigate_ui: Live view, review, explore and recordings of the Frigate cameras ticked below, and no others. No settings, no deleting, no exports, no camera control.
data_description.frigate_ui_url: Not the address the Frigate integration uses: on port 5000 Frigate treats everyone as administrator. Usually https, same host, port 8971.
data_description.frigate_ui_user: Make it in Frigate (Settings → Users) with a role limited to the cameras to show. Never an administrator. What that role may see is what visitors see; if it can see a camera this link does not publish, the Frigate panel shows nothing.

more_views.title: Which views of {dashboard}?
more_views.description: Every view is ticked to begin with. A view you add to **{dashboard}** later is not published until you tick it here.

error.invalid_path: Use 2-48 characters: lowercase letters, digits and underscores only (no hyphen).
error.path_reserved: That path is reserved by Home Assistant.
error.path_in_use: That path already belongs to a panel or dashboard. Choosing it would hide part of your Home Assistant.
error.path_taken: Another link already has that address, or one that begins the same way.
error.frigate_missing: Fill in Frigate's address, the user and the password, or switch the Frigate interface off.
error.frigate_cannot_connect: Frigate could not be reached at that address (expected: https, port 8971).
error.frigate_invalid_auth: Frigate did not accept that user name and password.
error.frigate_is_admin: That Frigate account is an administrator. Use one with a role limited to the cameras to show.

abort.no_dashboards: No dashboard has a saved configuration yet. Create a dashboard, add cards, save it, then set this up.

init.title: Link settings
init.description:
Your dashboard is published through Home Assistant's own frontend, live and read-only: visitors see exactly the views you chose and cannot change anything. Changing the public path takes effect after a Home Assistant restart.

**Time limit of this link now: {life}**

data_description.support_views: For cards that reuse something from another tab: reference cards, popups, a 3D floor plan whose popups show cards kept elsewhere. A supporting view has no tab, but a visitor who looks for it can read it, so it must hold nothing private.
data_description.title: Shown in the browser tab instead of the dashboard's own name and your home's name. Empty: the dashboard's name.
data_description.camera_streams: Only for cameras on a published view. Off: those cameras show still pictures.
data_description.frigate_cameras: Events, snapshots, clips and recordings of these cameras can be opened by cards on the published views. Cameras whose camera entity or name is on a published view are included without being listed here; every other camera stays closed.
data_description.hide_location: Home Assistant's frontend is normally told where the home is. On: visitors' browsers get 0, 0 instead. A card that centres on the home (a weather radar) then shows the wrong place; switch this off if your published views show where the home is anyway.
data_description.enabled: Off: the link is revoked. Its address answers 'not found' and everyone looking is disconnected at once. There is also a switch entity for this.
data_description.valid_for: The boxes are days, hours, minutes, seconds. For example 7 in the first box for a week. When set, it replaces the date below and counts from the moment you save.
data_description.expires_at: Empty: the link does not end by itself. From that moment the address answers 'not found' and everyone looking is disconnected.
data_description.frigate_ui: Live view, review, explore and recordings of the Frigate cameras ticked below, and no others. No settings, no deleting, no exports, no camera control.
data_description.more_dashboards: Each is shown whole unless you choose its views in the next step.
data_description.frigate_ui_url: Not the address the Frigate integration uses: on port 5000 Frigate treats everyone as administrator. Usually https, same host, port 8971.
data_description.frigate_ui_user: Make it in Frigate (Settings → Users) with a role limited to the cameras to show. Never an administrator. What that role may see is what visitors see; if it can see a camera this link does not publish, the Frigate panel shows nothing.
data_description.no_expiry: The link then lasts until you switch it off. Overrides the two fields above.
